If A and B pick same task, then only 3 distinct tasks possible (C and D will pick two other distinct tasks, total distinct = 3). So to maximize distinct tasks, A and B should pick different tasks.

Thus B should choose a task different from what A likely picks. Since we don't know A's choice, we need to anticipate A's rational choice given shared objective. Both A and B have same objective, they will try to coordinate to get 4 distinct tasks and minimize total cost.

They will choose assignment that minimizes total cost = cost_C(task_i)+cost_D(task_j). Since there are only two tasks, they can either assign C->task_i, D->task_j or C->task_j, D->task_i. Choose the lower sum.

Thus for remaining tasks {R1,R2}, total cost for C+D = min( cost_C(R1)+cost_D(R2), cost_C(R2)+cost_D(R1) ).
